chapter: Wider talk: bands, places and players
title: Dance lessons in the Pollack band, and unpaid jobs
summary: The Pollack band studied dancing for vaudeville; he says he never learned tap and recalls unpaid jobs.

story.theme_name: Getting paid: wages, tips and leaving over money
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: I, I didn't do any tap dance in the meantime. We studied, when, when, when, when, when, with Pollock, Pollock's band, we decided we were going to do some vaudeville, and, and, and we had, uh, some guy come in to show us how to dance, and we were going to do a dance, and do, I don't know. Pollock, Horace Heights band was the big thing at the time. You understand? Mm-hmm. You know, those guys, they, they, they didn't, they couldn't blow their nose. I mean, it's, I'm concerned. And, and everything at that time was, was, when, when, when, when, I don't know, when television was first come out or something, but it was, music was in their eyes at that time. You know, when you go to a show, you got to see what's happening on the stage and so forth. So, so Pollock wanted one of the guys to do things, uh, besides play instruments, you know. Mm-hmm. So we started, started dancing. Benny Goodman was dancing, you know, and things like that. We studied dancing.

But I never, I, all, all the, it was a time step and stuff like that, but I could never get into the thing. I did a, a, a slow, a slow, uh, snakeship dance. Mm-hmm. That, that, that's the only thing I haven't done anything. Somebody talked to me about mules.
Did you ever hear of mules? When somebody would give you the mule? The mule. Yeah, that means when they didn't pay you.
Oh, I, I don't know the expression.
I don't remember that expression at all.
Well, there's a lot of jobs that, that, that we, that I played in my life that I didn't get paid for, I'll tell you that. Yeah. But, uh, I, I didn't, uh, I don't remember that expression.
